Swimmer Plot: Patient Timelines, Response and Follow-up

Serdar Balci

2026-10-23

Source: vignettes/swimmerplot-unified-comprehensive.Rmd
swimmerplot-unified-comprehensive.Rmd

What a Swimmer Plot Is For

A swimmer plot draws one horizontal lane per patient, from the start to the end of their time on study, so a reader can see at once who stayed on treatment, for how long, and what happened along the way. In jamovi the analysis is under OncoPath → Patient Follow-Up Plots → Swimmer Plot; in R it is swimmerplot().

Besides the plot, the analysis reports:

  • the objective response rate (ORR, CR + PR) and disease control rate (DCR, CR + PR + SD) with exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% confidence intervals, over every patient in the analysis;
  • median follow-up: the reverse Kaplan-Meier estimate (Schemper and Smith 1996) when you supply a censoring status, otherwise the plain median of the observed durations, labelled as such;
  • person-time by best response, a milestone summary and an event-marker summary.

The swimmer plot is descriptive. Response rates are only as good as the response categories you supply, and person-time split by best response is biased by construction (a patient must live long enough to be assessed as a responder).

The Example Data

swimmerplot_sample is a synthetic dataset of 20 patients. Times are in months from the start of treatment.

library(OncoPath)
data(swimmerplot_sample, package = "OncoPath")
head(swimmerplot_sample, 4)
#>   PatientID StartTime EndTime Response Surgery TreatmentStart ResponseAssessment Progression       EventType EventTime
#> 1     PT001         0      24       CR       1              2                  6          NA Treatment Start         2
#> 2     PT002         0      18       PR       2              3                  6          12 Treatment Start         3
#> 3     PT003         0      22       SD       1              2                  6          16 Treatment Start         2
#> 4     PT004         0      15       PD       3              4                  8          10 Treatment Start         4

A Basic Swimmer Plot 

res <- swimmerplot(
  data        = swimmerplot_sample,
  patientID   = "PatientID",
  startTime   = "StartTime",
  endTime     = "EndTime",
  responseVar = "Response",
  timeUnit    = "months"
)
res$advancedMetrics$asDF[, c("metric_name", "metric_value", "confidence_interval")]

With these data the analysis reports 5 CR, 6 PR, 6 SD and 3 PD among 20 patients:

                                                         metric_name metric_value confidence_interval
Median Follow-up Time (observed durations; no censoring information)       19.5
                            Interquartile Range (observed durations)        7.5
                                             Total Study Person-Time      391.0
                                       Objective Response Rate (ORR)       55.0         31.5 - 76.9
                                          Disease Control Rate (DCR)       85.0         62.1 - 96.8

ORR and DCR are shown only when every response value is a RECIST category (CR, PR, SD, PD or NE; “complete/partial remission” are read as CR/PR). A coding such as Response / Stable / Progression withholds them, and a notice names the value that could not be read. When a patient has several response rows, the category used is the best response recorded up to the first PD; it carries no confirmation of CR/PR and no minimum duration for SD, and the output says so.

Milestones and Events

Up to five milestone variables can be added; each holds the time (or date) at which that milestone happened for each patient. The milestone name defaults to the variable’s own name.

res_ms <- swimmerplot(
  data        = swimmerplot_sample,
  patientID   = "PatientID",
  startTime   = "StartTime",
  endTime     = "EndTime",
  responseVar = "Response",
  milestone1Name = "Surgery",             milestone1Date = "Surgery",
  milestone2Name = "Treatment start",     milestone2Date = "TreatmentStart",
  milestone3Name = "Response assessment", milestone3Date = "ResponseAssessment",
  milestone4Name = "Progression",         milestone4Date = "Progression"
)
res_ms$milestoneTable$asDF
#>        milestone_name n_events median_time    time_range
#> 1         Progression        9          14 9 - 18 months
#> 2 Response assessment       20           6  6 - 8 months
#> 3             Surgery       20           2  1 - 3 months
#> 4     Treatment start       20           3  2 - 4 months

Event markers (showEventMarkers = TRUE, with eventVar for the event type and eventTimeVar for its time) add a point per event to the lanes.

Censoring and Follow-up

Without a censoring status, a lane that ends because follow-up ended looks the same as one that ends because the event occurred, and median follow-up can only be the median of the observed durations, which understates follow-up when events are common. Supply a status column with censorVar to draw status arrows on the patients still at risk and to estimate follow-up by the reverse Kaplan-Meier method.

How the status column is read is set with censorCoding:

censorCoding Reads
"auto" (default) numeric 0/1 (1 = event) and the words alive/censored/dead/event
"yes_event" / "yes_censored" Yes/TRUE = event, or Yes/TRUE = censored
"one_censored" 0/1 with 1 = censored
"two_event" / "one_event" 1/2 with 2 = event, or 1 = event

Yes/No, TRUE/FALSE and 1/2 columns are never read in a guessed direction: until you choose a coding, no arrows are drawn. Words such as “Completed”, “Progressed” or “Active” describe treatment or disease, not follow-up status; recode such a column first. Every reading is stated in a notice.

swimmerplot_sample has no status column. The example below adds one for illustration only (1 = died, 0 = alive at the data cut-off):

sw <- swimmerplot_sample
sw$Status <- as.integer(sw$PatientID %in% c("PT003", "PT004", "PT010", "PT011", "PT015", "PT019"))

res_cens <- swimmerplot(
  data        = sw,
  patientID   = "PatientID",
  startTime   = "StartTime",
  endTime     = "EndTime",
  responseVar = "Response",
  censorVar   = "Status"          # 0/1, read automatically with 1 = event
)
# Median Follow-up Time (reverse Kaplan-Meier): 23.0 months (95% CI 20.0 - not reached)

Groups, Dates and Display

  • groupVar names one fixed patient-level grouping variable (for example the treatment arm) for between-group comparisons. A patient whose episodes carry different groups stops the comparison, because episode-specific treatments cannot define independent patient groups.
  • timeType = "datetime" reads start, end and milestone columns as dates, using dateFormat (for example "ymd"); timeUnit then sets the unit the durations are shown in.
  • timeDisplay switches between time from each patient’s own start ("relative") and calendar time ("absolute").
  • referenceLines adds the median duration, protocol times (3/6/9/12/18/24/36 months) or a custom time (customReferenceTime).
  • sortVariable and sortOrder order the lanes; laneWidth, markerSize, plotTheme, colorPalette and showLegend control the look.
  • showGlossary, showCopyReady and showAbout add a glossary, paste-ready sentences and a description of the method; exportTimeline and exportSummary add exportable tables.

Reference

Schemper M, Smith TL. A note on quantifying follow-up in studies of failure time. Control Clin Trials. 1996;17(4):343-346.
